title: Recall Quiz: Rise of the Novel: Addison & Fielding

questions.q: Which two writers famously collaborated on the periodical 'The Spectator'?
questions.explanation: Addison and Steele were the leading figures of the periodical essay movement.

questions.q: A novel written entirely as a series of documents or letters is known as:
questions.explanation: Epistolary novels, popularized by Richardson, are composed of letters.

questions.q: Which novel, often considered the first true English novel, details the 28-year survival of a castaway on an island?
questions.explanation: Daniel Defoe's Robinson Crusoe (1719) is a landmark in literary realism.

questions.q: Henry Fielding's 'Tom Jones' follows the episodic adventures of a wandering, lovable rogue. This genre is called:
questions.explanation: The picaresque novel (from the Spanish 'picaro' meaning rogue) details the episodic journey of a lower-class hero.

questions.q: Henry Fielding wrote 'Shamela' as a direct, mocking parody of which highly moralistic novel?
questions.explanation: Fielding found Richardson's 'Pamela' hypocritical and parodied it with 'Shamela'.

questions.q: The rise of the English novel in the 18th century was closely linked to the growth of which social class?
questions.explanation: The growing middle class (bourgeoisie) desired realistic literature reflecting their own lives.

questions.q: Who among the following is NOT considered one of the 'Four Wheels of the English Novel'?
questions.explanation: While Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels (a satire), the 'Four Wheels' are Defoe, Richardson, Fielding, and Smollett.

questions.q: Sir Roger de Coverley is a famous fictional character associated with which publication?
questions.explanation: He was a prominent member of the fictional club in Addison and Steele's 'The Spectator'.
